articles.title: Aborto, armas, direitos trans, taxa para bilionários: eleições nos EUA tem referendos em 39 estados | G1
articles.standfirst: Consultas populares podem alterar leis e Constituições estaduais nas eleições de 3 de novembro; propostas incluem restrições ao aborto, mudanças nas regras eleitorais e tributos sobre bilionários.
articles.summary: Consultas populares podem alterar leis e Constituições estaduais nas eleições de 3 de novembro; propostas incluem restrições ao aborto, mudanças nas regras eleitorais e tributos sobre bilionários.
articles.body:
Além de definir a nova composição do Congresso, as eleições de meio de mandato dos Estados Unidos , conhecidas como midterms , também permitirão que os eleitores decidam diretamente em seus estados sobre questões como armas, aborto e direitos das pessoas trans.

Ao todo, 145 propostas estaduais serão submetidas ao voto popular, em consultas conhecidas como ballot measures, em inglês.

➡️ Os referendos podem criar novas leis, modificar regras existentes ou revogar políticas aprovadas anteriormente.

Na votação marcada para a próxima terça-feira (3), os cidadãos americanos de 39 estados vão deliberar sobre temas como aborto, impostos, regras eleitorais, direitos de pessoas transgênero e justiça criminal . A Califórnia e o Colorado concentram o maior número de propostas estaduais, com 14 cada.

Eleitores votam nas eleições presidenciais dos EUA em Madison, Wisconsin, em 5 de novembro de 2024. — Foto: AP Photo/Kayla Wolf

Quatro estados devem votar propostas relacionadas ao direito ao aborto.

Em Idaho , Nevada e Virgínia , as medidas buscam estabelecer ou ampliar proteções legais ao procedimento;

No Missouri , a proposta pretende revogar uma garantia aprovada pelos eleitores em 2024 e restringir o acesso à interrupção de gravidez.

Os eleitores do Idaho decidirão se o estado deve reconhecer legalmente o direito ao aborto até a viabilidade fetal, por volta das 24 semanas de gestação. Atualmente, o estado tem uma das proibições mais rigorosas do país.

Em Nevada, os habitantes votarão pela segunda vez em uma emenda constitucional para proteger o direito ao aborto até a viabilidade fetal e preservação da vida e da saúde da gestante. A proposta já recebeu apoio nas urnas em 2024, mas precisa ser aprovada novamente para entrar na Constituição estadual.

Na Virgínia, a consulta busca incluir na Constituição estadual o direito à liberdade reprodutiva. A proteção abrangeria o aborto antes do terceiro trimestre e, depois desse período, em situações previstas na proposta, como quando há riscos à mulher.

No Missouri, o referendo segue o caminho oposto. Se aprovada, a medida revogará a proteção constitucional à liberdade reprodutiva aprovada em 2024 e permitirá restrições mais severas ao aborto, com exceções específicas. A proposta também prevê proibir determinados procedimentos médicos de transição de gênero para menores de idade.

Eleitores de diferentes estados vão deliberar as propostas que afetam pessoas trans, principalmente em competições esportivas escolares e no acesso a tratamentos médicos.

Arizona , Colorado , Nebraska e Washington votarão medidas para restringir a participação de meninas e mulheres trans em equipes esportivas femininas. As regras propostas variam entre os estados e incluem exigências de verificação do sexo biológico.

No Arizona , a proposta também prevê restrições ao uso de banheiros e vestiários em escolas de acordo com a identidade de gênero, com base no sexo registrado na certidão de nascimento.

No Missouri e no Colorado , os eleitores também decidirão sobre restrições a procedimentos médicos de afirmação de gênero para menores de idade.

Os eleitores de Idaho e Massachusetts também devem votar sobre armas de fogo.

Em Idaho , a consulta pergunta qual entre seis armas históricas deve ser escolhida como a arma oficial do estado . A proposta, apresentada por parlamentares republicanos, não é vinculante e busca incentivar a participação nas eleições de meio de mandato.

Em Massachusetts , os eleitores decidirão se mantêm uma lei aprovada em 2024 que ampliou as restrições a armas de fogo . A legislação exige o registro de armas no estado e proíbe armas sem número de série e dispositivos que permitem disparos rápidos.

A lei também ampliou os mecanismos que permitem solicitar à Justiça a retirada temporária de armas de pessoas consideradas um risco para si mesmas ou para terceiros. A consulta foi convocada após opositores reunirem assinaturas para tentar revogar as regras.

Justiça criminal: endurecimento de penas

Propostas para endurecer a legislação penal também estarão nas urnas. Seis medidas em cinco estados — Alabama, Colorado, Indiana, Louisiana e Tennessee — tratam de mudanças nas regras de fiança e no aumento de penas para determinados crimes.

No Colorado , uma das propostas prevê prisão perpétua sem possibilidade de liberdade condicional para pessoas condenadas por tráfico de menores.

As propostas refletem disputas sobre punição criminal, segurança pública e o alcance das penas previstas nas leis estaduais.

Regras eleitorais e exigência de cidadania

Seis estados votarão medidas para incluir em suas leis ou Constituições estaduais a exigência de cidadania americana para votar em eleições estaduais e locais. São eles Alasca, Arizona, Arkansas, Kansas, Dakota do Sul e Virgínia Ocidental.

A legislação federal já proíbe que não cidadãos votem em eleições federais . As propostas estaduais buscam explicitar a restrição também nas regras locais e estaduais.

Outros seis estados votarão propostas relacionadas à identificação dos eleitores. Arizona, Califórnia, Colorado, Nevada, Carolina do Norte e Ohio discutem mudanças que podem exigir documentos oficiais ou informações adicionais para votar presencialmente ou pelo correio.

As exigências variam conforme o estado. Algumas propostas preveem a apresentação de documento com foto; outras tratam do fornecimento de números de identificação, como os últimos dígitos da carteira de motorista ou do número de seguridade social.

➡️ Defensores das medidas afirmam que as mudanças reforçam a segurança eleitoral. Críticos argumentam que exigências adicionais podem dificultar o acesso às urnas.

Impostos sobre bilionários e mudanças tributárias

Os impostos estão entre os principais temas das consultas populares deste ano. Mais de vinte propostas em diferentes estados tratam de tributos sobre renda, patrimônio e imóveis.

Na Califórnia , uma das propostas prevê um imposto extra de 5% sobre o patrimônio de determinados bilionários residentes no estado. A arrecadação seria destinada a programas de saúde, educação e assistência alimentar.

Outra medida busca tornar permanente uma alíquota adicional do imposto sobre rendas elevadas, cuja vigência está prevista para terminar em 2031. O dinheiro arrecadado é destinado ao financiamento de programas de educação e saúde

O governador da Califórnia, Gavin Newsom, se opõe ao imposto sobre bilionários. Entre as preocupações levantadas por críticos da proposta está a possibilidade de que pessoas muito ricas transfiram sua residência para outros estados, reduzindo a arrecadação futura.

Em Washington , os eleitores decidirão se revogam um imposto de 9,9% sobre rendas milionárias , aprovado em março.

Já na Flórida , uma proposta busca ampliar a isenção de impostos sobre imóveis residenciais para tributos que não financiam escolas. A mudança reduziria a cobrança para proprietários, mas também poderia diminuir os recursos disponíveis para serviços públicos locais.

articles.title: Pré-natal odontológico ajuda a prevenir problemas na gravidez | G1
articles.standfirst: Alterações hormonais, enjoos e mudanças na alimentação podem afetar dentes e gengivas durante a gestação; especialistas explicam cuidados, riscos e direitos garantidos pelo SUS.
articles.summary: Saúde bucal na gravidez: especialistas explicam a importância do pré-natal odontológico, os riscos da falta de cuidado e os direitos das gestantes no SUS.
articles.body:
Ana Cecília com o primeiro filho no colo e grávida do segundo — Foto: Reprodução

A gravidez costuma vir acompanhada de uma lista de cuidados que preocupam as gestantes. Consultas de pré-natal, exames, alimentação equilibrada e mudanças na rotina são alguns dos pontos mais observados a partir da descoberta de uma gravidez. Mas existe uma parte da saúde que merece receber a mesma atenção durante esse período: a saúde bucal.

Grávida de quatro meses do segundo filho, Rafael, Ana Cecília, de 33 anos, já conhecia a importância dos cuidados com a saúde bucal durante a gestação. Médica otorrinolaringologista, ela mantém o acompanhamento odontológico preventivo, com consultas para limpeza e avaliação, mesmo sem apresentar sintomas.

“Antes de engravidar, eu já sabia que precisava, sim, de atenção à saúde bucal. Eu sou médica e já sabia dessa importância, da profilaxia. Nunca tive nenhum sintoma gengival, mas faço esse acompanhamento odontológico justamente para limpezas e verificação de como é que está”, conta.

Ana não teve problemas odontológicos nem sofreu com enjoos ou vômitos, que podem dificultar a escovação durante a gravidez. No entanto, ela percebeu mudanças na rotina alimentar. Por ter diabetes, passou a sentir mais fome e a diminuir os intervalos entre as refeições, o que reforçou a necessidade de manter os cuidados com os dentes.

“Como sou diabética, comecei a ter mais fome, então encurtei os intervalos das refeições. Isso acaba facilitando o acúmulo de tártaro e dando mais vontade de comer doces. Por isso, é importante ter uma atenção especial”, relata.

Durante a gravidez, alterações hormonais influenciam diretamente na saúde da mulher. Tais mudanças podem provocar inflamações na gengiva, especialmente quando há acúmulo de placa bacteriana. Enjoos e episódios de vômito também podem exigir atenção redobrada à higiene oral. Por isso, o acompanhamento odontológico é parte importante do cuidado integral com a gestante.

Durante o primeiro trimestre da gestação, a náusea é um mal-estar que pode estar mais presente. A gestante pode sentir uma sensibilidade nos dentes e mau hálito, e por esse motivo, muitas mulheres sentem um maior incômodo durante a escovação.

Ellen Emanuella, de 32 anos, relembra que enfrentou dificuldades durante a gestação do quarto filho. Na primeira gravidez, a agricultora não teve acompanhamento odontológico, apesar de ter realizado o pré-natal.

Ellen Emanuella da Silva durante a gravidez — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

“Como foi a primeira gravidez, era tudo muito novo pra mim. Teve, sim, o pré-natal completo, mas não tive atendimento com dentistas”, conta.

A partir da segunda gestação, o cenário mudou, e Ellen passou a ser acompanhada por um profissional de saúde bucal. Por meio do atendimento especializado na rede pública, ela conseguiu realizar procedimentos odontológicos que ajudaram a melhorar seu bem-estar durante a gravidez.

Durante o as consultas, a agricultora recebeu orientações para manter os cuidados com a saúde bucal em dia e procurar um dentista regularmente. Ela precisou fazer uma restauração, que ajudou a diminuir a sensibilidade nos dentes e a dor ao mastigar.

“Senti muita diferença na hora de comer. Antes eu tinha bastante sensibilidade com água gelada e dor para mastigar de um lado da boca. Com o início dos cuidados [bucais], conseguia me alimentar normalmente sem nenhum incômodo”, disse Ellen.

De acordo com Mariana Cordeiro, especialista em odontopediatria, a falta de cuidados com a saúde bucal e os maus hábitos de higiene podem favorecer problemas que exigem atenção durante a gestação. Uma mulher que consome muito açúcar e não mantém uma rotina adequada de higiene bucal, por exemplo, tem maior risco de desenvolver cáries.

Problemas nas gengivas, como o granuloma gravídico, também podem surgir durante a gravidez. A lesão é benigna, avermelhada e apresenta grande quantidade de vasos sanguíneos. Ela aparece com mais frequência na gengiva e pode estar relacionada às variações hormonais desse período.

“Muito se fala de infecção urinária durante a gestação e de suas complicações, mas sabemos que todas as infecções durante esse período merecem atenção. Durante a gestação, a mulher passa por muitas mudanças, uma delas é a inflamação na gengiva, a periodontite, que é quando a gengiva fica mais inchada, mais vermelha e sangrando com mais facilidade”, explica a odontopediatra.

Mariana Cordeiro, especialista em Odontopediatria — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Durante a gestação, o aumento dos níveis de estrogênio e progesterona podem deixar a gengiva mais sensível à placa bacteriana, favorecendo a inflamação e o sangramento.

“Existem estudos que associam doenças periodontais ao parto prematuro, baixo peso ao nascer e pré-eclâmpsia. Embora não exista comprovação de uma relação direta de causa e efeito, sabemos que infecções e inflamações importantes precisam ser tratadas para poder proteger a saúde materna e fetal”, esclarece a médica Daniele Aragão, ginecologista e obstetra.

A médica ainda alerta que os hábitos de higiene e alimentação da mãe influenciam diretamente os cuidados com a criança. Por isso, cuidar da saúde bucal durante a gestação também é investir na saúde do bebê.

Especialistas explicam ainda que os primeiros mil dias de vida, período que compreende a gestação e os dois primeiros anos da criança, são considerados fundamentais para o desenvolvimento infantil e também para a saúde bucal.

“O ideal é começar o acompanhamento de pré-natal odontológico assim que descobrir a gestação, será um momento de realizar os procedimentos odontológicos necessários, mas também um período de orientação para o cuidado do bebê que está chegando”, disse Mariana Cordeiro.

Após o nascimento do bebê, o indicado é realizar o teste da linguinha para identificar a necessidade de alguma intervenção para facilitar o aleitamento materno. Depois da consulta, deve ser feito o acompanhamento semestral.

A Constituição Federal garante a saúde como direito de todos os cidadãos e dever do Estado. O Estatuto da Criança e do Adolescente, por meio do artigo 8º, assegura à gestante atendimento pré-natal integral pelo SUS. A Lei nº 14.572/2023 instituiu a Política Nacional de Saúde Bucal em lei e incluiu a saúde bucal entre as obrigações do SUS.

Dados da Secretaria Estadual de Saúde mostram que em Pernambuco foram registradas 655.233 consultas de pré-natal na rede pública de Atenção Primária à Saúde em 2025. Já em 2026, considerando os dados disponíveis de janeiro a agosto, foram contabilizadas 505.339 consultas.

Os quantitativos de consultas não representam o número de gestantes distintas atendidas, uma vez que cada mulher pode realizar múltiplas consultas durante o acompanhamento pré-natal.

Em entrevista ao g1 , a advogada Fernanda Martins, especialista em Direito Médico e da Saúde e presidente da Comissão de Direito Médico e da Saúde da Ordem dos Advogados do Brasil, subseção de Caruaru, explica que não existe uma única “lei do dentista na gravidez”.

“Desde a Constituição de 1988, o SUS deve oferecer atendimento integral, e o Estatuto da Criança e do Adolescente, de 1990, garante à gestante um pré-natal completo. Em 2004, a política Brasil Sorridente colocou as grávidas como público prioritário da saúde bucal. A garantia ficou expressa em 2024, quando a Rede Alyne, programa do Ministério da Saúde para a saúde da mãe e do bebê, incluiu no pré-natal o cuidado integral com a saúde bucal da gestante”, disse a advogada.

articles.title: França tem novo dia de protestos e teme confrontos e saques | G1
articles.standfirst: Autoridades preveem cerca de 150 manifestações em todo o país. Em Paris, estações de metrô foram fechadas e comerciantes protegeram vitrines diante do temor de violência e saques.
articles.summary: Autoridades preveem cerca de 150 manifestações em todo o país. Em Paris, estações de metrô foram fechadas e comerciantes protegeram vitrines diante do temor de violência e saques.
articles.body:
A França enfrenta neste sábado (31) uma nova jornada de manifestações contra o custo de vida e em defesa de melhores condições de estudo para estudantes do ensino médio e universitários. O país mobilizou 70 mil policiais e agentes de segurança em todo o território, diante do temor de novos confrontos, após os episódios de violência e saques registrados em 17 de outubro.

Em Paris, a tensão é particularmente elevada. O Conselho de Estado, a mais alta instância administrativa francesa, decidiu durante a madrugada alterar o trajeto da principal manifestação prevista para a capital. O percurso inicialmente anunciado entre Bastilha e Nação, no centro de Paris, foi substituído por um itinerário entre Porta de Bagnolet e Porta de Charenton, na periferia da cidade.

A decisão foi tomada diante do que o tribunal classificou como um “risco muito elevado de novos distúrbios graves à ordem pública”. A manifestação havia sido autorizada em parte por um tribunal administrativo de Paris, mas o governo recorreu, e o Conselho de Estado acabou dando razão à prefeitura e ao Ministério do Interior.

O receio é que os protestos deste sábado reproduzam as cenas registradas em 17 de outubro, quando manifestações contra o custo de vida e em apoio às reivindicações estudantis foram acompanhadas por confrontos com a polícia, saques de lojas e incêndios em prédios públicos. A mobilização de 24 de outubro, por sua vez, transcorreu de maneira muito mais tranquila: segundo o Ministério do Interior, 410 mil pessoas participaram dos protestos em todo o país, sendo 110 mil em Paris.

O movimento reúne grupos de origens distintas, entre eles ativistas dos coletes amarelos, sindicatos e estudantes do ensino médio e universitários. As reivindicações inicialmente se concentravam no aumento do custo de vida, na desigualdade social e na deterioração das condições de ensino.

Depois dos confrontos e da resposta policial, porém, as reivindicações se ampliaram. Parte dos manifestantes passou a denunciar também restrições ao direito de protestar e exigir maior proteção às liberdades civis.

O governo, por sua vez, afirma que continuará garantindo o direito de manifestação, mas considera prioritário impedir novos episódios de violência. O ministro francês do Interior, Laurent Nuñez, classificou o risco de distúrbios para este sábado como “muito elevado”.

As autoridades também realizaram operações preventivas desde a noite de sexta-feira, especialmente em estradas, estações ferroviárias e centros urbanos, para apreender objetos que poderiam ser utilizados em atos de violência. Em Mulhouse, no leste do país, foram apreendidos 175 artefatos pirotécnicos, segundo o Ministério do Interior.

A coincidência da manifestação com o Halloween acrescentou uma preocupação às autoridades: a possibilidade de que participantes utilizem fantasias ou máscaras para esconder o rosto.

O Ministério do Interior lembrou que a legislação francesa proíbe esconder o rosto em uma manifestação quando há distúrbios ou razões para acreditar que eles possam ocorrer. O governo também alertou contra o porte de armas ou objetos que possam ser utilizados como armas, mesmo quando fazem parte de uma fantasia.

Manifestante joga objeto contra policiais na França — Foto: Stephanie Lecocq/Reuters

Segundo o ministro do Interior, mensagens publicadas nas redes sociais convocaram pessoas para encontros durante a noite e chegaram a utilizar expressões como “revolução” e “noite de escuridão”. As autoridades temem que grupos violentos possam se aproveitar das manifestações ou das comemorações de Halloween.

O impacto sobre a circulação na capital é significativo. As primeiras interdições começaram ainda de madrugada, em áreas como Champs-Élysées, Concorde, Invalides e Assembleia Nacional. Ao longo da manhã, as restrições avançaram para République, Châtelet e Les Halles e, posteriormente, para regiões próximas a Nation, Porte Dorée, Saint-Germain-des-Prés, Odéon e Quartier Latin.

A circulação de bondes também foi interrompida em determinados trechos das linhas T3a e T3b, principalmente na região de Porta de Vincennes.

Empresas de bicicletas e patinetes compartilhados também adotaram medidas preventivas. Áreas próximas ao trajeto das manifestações foram temporariamente bloqueadas para circulação e estacionamento, e veículos foram retirados durante a madrugada.

Mulher segura placa dizendo "A França disse não" durante protestos em 16 de março de 2023 — Foto: Daniel Cole/AP

A nova jornada de protestos ocorre em um momento de forte tensão política na França, a cerca de seis meses da eleição presidencial. O ambiente social já vinha sendo marcado por manifestações e confrontos, e o presidente Emmanuel Macron reconheceu nesta semana que não é normal que o país esteja mergulhado em tamanha turbulência tão próximo de uma eleição.

O crescimento da insatisfação também ocorre em um cenário de avanço da direita radical nas pesquisas de opinião. Marine Le Pen, líder do partido de extrema direita Reunião Nacional, aparece na liderança de pesquisas para a próxima eleição presidencial.

O governo tenta evitar que os protestos se transformem em uma crise política mais ampla. Para as autoridades, o desafio deste sábado é permitir que as manifestações ocorram sem que o movimento seja novamente acompanhado por violência, saques e depredações.

Para os organizadores, porém, a mudança do percurso em Paris representa uma restrição ao direito de manifestação. A CGT, uma das principais centrais sindicais francesas, criticou a decisão do governo e afirmou que a alteração do trajeto pode desorganizar a mobilização.

Homem caminha diante de fogo em meio a manifestação em Paris, em 18 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Abdul Saboor/ Reuters

articles.title: Dia de Finados: cemitérios de São Luís terão horário ampliado e programação religiosa | G1
articles.standfirst: Os cemitérios funcionarão das 6h às 18h na segunda-feira (2). Também estão previstas celebrações religiosas e medidas especiais de segurança para receber os visitantes.
articles.summary: Os cemitérios funcionarão das 6h às 18h na segunda-feira (2). Também estão previstas celebrações religiosas e medidas especiais de segurança para receber os visitantes.
articles.body:
Cemitérios de São Luís terão horário ampliado e programação religiosa — Foto: João Ricardo Barbosa / G1

Os cemitérios de São Luís terão horário de funcionamento estendido nesta segunda-feira (2), Dia de Finados. Segundo a Secretaria Municipal de Urbanismo e Habitação (Semurh), os locais estarão abertos das 6h às 18h para receber familiares e visitantes que pretendem prestar homenagens aos entes queridos.

Além da visitação, os cemitérios terão uma programação religiosa especial, com celebrações organizadas pela Igreja Católica e participação de representantes de outras denominações religiosas.

De acordo com a Semurh, as atividades religiosas seguirão uma programação previamente organizada. Também estão previstas medidas de segurança para garantir a organização dos espaços e o acolhimento dos visitantes.

A secretaria orienta que os visitantes planejem a ida aos cemitérios com antecedência e sigam as recomendações das equipes responsáveis pelos locais.

articles.title: Amiga diz que pecuarista insistiu em enconto com jovem antes do crime | G1
articles.standfirst: Priscila Lacerda foi acompanhada pela amiga e pelo irmão até Rifaina (SP), para devolver a caminhonete do pecuarista João Roberto Bolelli. A amiga sugeriu que eles deixassem o carro na cidade, mas o homem convenceu a jovem a se encontrarem pessoalmente e a baleou durante uma discussão.
articles.summary: Priscila Lacerda foi acompanhada pela amiga e pelo irmão até Rifaina (SP), para devolver a caminhonete do pecuarista João Roberto Bolelli. Ela foi morta pelo homem com um tiro.
articles.body:
Pollyanna Botelho, amiga que presenciou o assassinato de Priscila Lacerda Custodio, disse, em entrevista ao g1 nesta sexta-feira (30), que o pecuarista insistiu com a jovem em encontrá-la pessoalmente para a entrega da caminhonete dele que estava com ela. A empresária, natural de Perdizes , no Alto Paranaíba, foi baleada por João Roberto Bolelli em Rifaina (SP), na noite da última terça-feira (27).

Priscila, de 24 anos, foi acompanhada pelo irmão e pela amiga até a cidade paulista para devolver o carro de Bolelli, com quem teve um relacionamento casual, pois estava apreensiva. Quatro dias antes do crime, a empresária tinha relatado à amiga que tinha sido agredida e ameaçada pelo pecuarista de 62 anos.

Segundo o boletim de ocorrência, ela encontrou João Roberto às margens da Rodovia Cândido Portinari (SP-334), próximo a uma propriedade rural.

Antes de se encontrarem, no entanto, Priscila não estava conseguindo localizar o ponto de encontro e Pollyanna sugeriu à amiga que elas deixassem a caminhonete na cidade, para que o próprio pecuarista fosse buscar o carro. A jovem não concordou com a ideia, pois tinha medo que o veículo pudesse ser furtado e, além disso, foi convencida pelo pecuarista a encontrá-lo pessoalmente.

"Ele mandou mensagem falando que não tinha como ir na cidade buscar [a caminhonete], porque ele não estava com nenhum automóvel, ele estava a pé. Ele insistiu com ela para que ela fosse até lá", disse ela.

Priscila seguia com Pollyanna no carro da amiga e o irmão dela, Geovane Santana, seguia na caminhonete do pecuarista. Ao chegarem no local de encontro, a jovem saiu do veículo e começou a conversar com Bolelli.

Os dois começaram a discutir sobre um suposto celular que ele teria dado a ela. Durante o desentendimento, o pecuarista sacou uma arma e atirou em Priscila. Ele fugiu após o crime e é investigado por feminicídio.

Na quarta-feira (28), a Justiça de São Paulo decretou a prisão preventiva do homem. Até a última atualização desta reportagem, o pecuarista não havia sido localizado e era considerado foragido pelas autoridades.

Priscila Lacerda Custodio foi morta a tiro por João Roberto Bolelli — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Amiga diz que pecuarista era 'controlador e ciumento'

Segundo Pollyanna, Priscila estava com a caminhonete de Bolelli devido a ameaças que ele tinha feito a ela. A jovem estava com pecuarista em Rifaina, quando foi agredida por ele na sexta-feira (23) e resolveu voltar para Perdizes.

O homem, que geralmente a buscava em Minas Gerais para ir para São Paulo e depois a levava de volta para casa, não quis que ela fosse embora.

"Ele entregou a caminhonete dele para ela, dizendo que era para ela retornar lá para a Rifaina no domingo, porque senão ele ia dar um tiro na cabeça dela. No domingo ela não foi porque foi domingo de eleição. Na segunda ela também não quis ir. Ela retornou na terça-feira por conta que ele estava ameaçando ela", contou a amiga.

A amiga afirma que Priscila e o pecuarista nunca tiveram um relacionamento, mas que tinham encontros casuais . Para o homem, no entanto, a relação era mais do que isso. "Ele queria ter posse dela. Ele queria ter ela só pra ele e não aceitava de forma nenhuma que ela interrompesse qualquer vínculo que existia", contou a amiga.

As duas eram amigas há cinco anos e moravam na mesma rua em Perdizes. Pollyanna, que é manicure e tem 31 anos, sabia do contato que a amiga tinha com o pecuarista há cerca de cinco meses. A amiga, porém, não sabe quando e como os dois se conheceram.

Segundo ela, a jovem já tentava terminar a relação casual há meses, desde quando começou a namorar Samuel Ramos, que era o atual companheiro dela. "Só que ele [o pecuarista], com a pressão psicológica que ele fazia, ela acabava cedendo em algumas coisas por medo, por ameaças. Mas desde quando ela conheceu o Samuel, ela já não queria mais envolvimento nenhum", afirmou Pollyanna.

"Ela continuou porque ele estava fazendo chantagem emocional com ela. 'Se você não vier me ver, eu vou acabar morrendo, porque eu estou muito doente, você tem que vir me ver. Eu dou para você o que você quiser, mas vem, por favor, cuidar de mim'. Ela não estava indo [até Rifaina] porque ela estava com ele, até porque eles não estavam juntos, nunca estiveram de verdade. Mas, ele fazia essa chantagem emocional para que ela pudesse ir ver ele."

Pollyanna acompanhou a amiga até Rifaina e presenciou o assassinato dela — Foto: Arquivo pessoal/Pollyanna Botelho

Priscila planejava comprar casa com o namorado

Priscila Lacerda planejava comprar uma casa em Uberlândia , no Triângulo Mineiro, para morar com o atual namorado Samuel Ramos, de 26 anos, segundo o relato dele ao g1. A jovem, que estudava de forma remota marketing digital e fotografia, era conhecida pelos amigos e familiares como uma pessoa dedicada e trabalhadora.

Segundo Samuel, a empresária já tinha terminado a relação casual com Bolelli quando os dois se conheceram. O homem, no entanto, não aceitava que ela se relacionasse com outra pessoa e chegou a contratar um detetive para segui-la, de acordo com o relato dele.

Ele e Priscila namoravam desde junho e moravam juntos há cerca de um mês em Perdizes. O casal se aproximou através da mãe dele, a psicóloga Fabyana Oliveira, que era amiga e cliente da jovem.

Priscila era empresária da área de marketing digital e também trabalhava como videomaker. Nas redes sociais, a jovem compartilhava os diversos trabalhos que fazia com lojas, casamentos e clientes.

"A Priscila era uma pessoa maravilhosa, cheia de sonhos e projetos. Cheia de vida! Uma vida que foi ceifada por um homem malvado", contou Fabyana ao g1.

A jovem também tinha muitas metas e não media esforços para alcançá-las, conforme o relato do namorado.

Priscila e Bolelli tinham uma relação casual desde o final de 2025, segundo Samuel. O pecuarista, no entanto, perseguiu a jovem após ela tentar terminar o relacionamento .

"Ele perseguia ela, porque ele se apaixonou por ela. Ela tinha rompido esses encontros esporádicos e ele não aceitava de maneira alguma. [...] Ele ameaçava ela, dizia que se ela não fosse ser dele, não seria de mais ninguém. Ele disse que ia dar um tiro na cabeça dela", afirmou o namorado.

Priscila Lacerda e Samuel Ramos; jovem de Perdizes morta por pecuarista em SP — Foto: Arquivo pessoal/Samuel Ramos

Crime foi presenciado pelo irmão de Priscila

Priscila foi acompanhada pelo irmão e por uma amiga até Rifaina (SP) para devolver o carro de Bolelli, pois estava apreensiva. No local, houve uma discussão entre os dois envolvendo um celular que ele teria dado a ela.

O irmão da vítima contou à polícia que a jovem disse que queria ir embora e não desejava continuar o relacionamento. Durante o desentendimento, Bolelli sacou uma arma e atirou contra Priscila. Ele fugiu na mesma caminhonete que a vítima tinha devolvido.

Ao g1 Ribeirão e Franca, a defesa de João disse que analisa o caso e ainda não teve contato com ele.

Priscila foi velada e sepultada em Perdizes, também na quarta-feira (28).

Caminhonete que Priscila foi a Rifaina devolver ao suspeito. Segundo o boletim, Bolelli fugiu no veículo após o crime — Foto: Câmera de segurança

Em depoimento à polícia, a amiga de Priscila que a acompanhou até Rifaina contou que a jovem mantinha um relacionamento casual com Bolelli desde julho.

Segundo a testemunha, Priscila relatou ter sido agredida pelo pecuarista na sexta-feira (23), quatro dias antes do crime. A amiga afirmou que viu as lesões apresentadas pela jovem.

Priscila também teria contado à amiga que Bolelli havia ameaçado dar um tiro na cabeça dela e contratado pessoas para monitorá-la. O pecuarista, ainda segundo o relato, acreditava que a jovem estivesse envolvida com outro homem e dizia que não permitiria que ela retornasse a Perdizes.

A amiga também disse à polícia que, diante das ameaças, orientou Priscila a não ir sozinha a Rifaina e, por isso, ela e o irmão da vítima decidiram acompanhá-la na devolução da caminhonete.

O irmão contou à polícia que recebeu uma ligação da jovem pedindo companhia para a viagem. Durante a conversa, percebeu que Priscila estava apreensiva e teve a impressão de que ela poderia estar sendo intimidada ou ameaçada.

Priscila Lacerda era empresária da área de marketing digital — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

articles.title: Newspaper headlines: 'Rush to recover stolen $6bn' and 'War on wind farms'
articles.summary: The theft of billions of dollars from Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, makes Saturday's front pages.
articles.body:
Warning: Saturday's paper review contains spoilers for The Celebrity Traitors.

The Daily Mail leads on further allegations against the Duchess of Sussex's father, Thomas Markle. Under the headline "Vault of Shame" the paper says it has reported Markle to the FBI after its journalists uncovered what it called a "stash" of child pornography in a storage unit the paper says was rented by him in Mexico.

The Sun says it has been told by staff at the care home where Thomas Markle has been living that he has been asked to leave, and is now staying at a different home, in Florida. Markle has strongly denied allegations that he has possessed images of child abuse.

In his Guardian article, Andy Burnham offers what the paper says amounts to a personal apology for Britain's role in the transatlantic slave trade. The prime minister says he will launch an initiative to help the Commonwealth's poorest countries repay their debts, over a longer period of time, with better rates. Ruling out financial reparations, Burnham says he does not think "British people today can be held liable for historical wrongs, however heinous".

Leading the Times, Chancellor John Healey vows to veto new clean energy projects, if there is a risk the grid cannot cope with the electricity generated pushing up costs for consumers. The chancellor says there is "no sense in building power that can't connect and then paying to switch it off". The paper's editorial notes that wind farms were allowed to connect to the network before upgrades to the national grid had been carried out.

The Daily Telegraph says several Red Wall Labour MPs are calling on the government to reduce the benefits bill, and not to appease what one calls the "leafy Surrey suburbs". Another MP tells the paper the government should be "ambitious", adding that the UK needed a "Beveridge report for the 21st century".

The Daily Mirror leads on a report that the King's niece , Zara Tindall, has a jewellery range that features gems from an Australian mine that has been criticised over pollution. "Zara and the Toxic Diamonds" is the headline. The paper says Zara Tindall's agent did not respond to a request for comment.

images.caption: The FT Weekend leads its coverage with the headline "Binance rush to recover stolen $6bn" looking at what it describes as the "largest heist in history". The "world's dominant crypto exchange" was apparently targeted by hackers from North Korea, the paper reports.

articles.title: Spain train disaster clouds Pedro Sánchez chances of re-election
articles.summary: The Spanish PM is hit by a succession of crises just weeks before a snap general election.
articles.body:
The breaking news from Spain this week was shocking but also shockingly familiar: another collision on the high-speed rail line south from Madrid, with reports of dozens killed.

It is just nine months since two trains crashed near Cordoba, killing 46 people. Now 69 bodies have been recovered here in central Spain, from wreckage strewn over the tracks and down an embankment.

For the victims' families it is devastating; a personal tragedy.

But it is also a national disaster that has shattered confidence in the country's rail network and the Socialist-led government of Pedro Sánchez. It is playing out just weeks before the snap general election he called.

The formal investigation into the Toledo train disaster has only just been launched but the government has been quick to take control of the narrative.

From the first hours after the collision, Transport Minister Oscar Puente began suggesting "human error" was to blame, batting responsibility as far as possible from the cabinet.

On Friday, he appeared before the press for a second time to set out what he called the "objective facts" of the crash and counter a surge of criticism against the government.

The opposition People's Party (PP) is among those calling for his resignation as a "moral" and "ethical" move.

Instead after expressing "huge pain and sadness" for the victims, Puente went on the offensive.

He rejected talk of chronic underinvestment in infrastructure and insisted that Spain's high-speed signalling safety system, the LZB, was neither old nor inadequate: Germany and Austria use the same.

In Spain, it has already failed 170 times so far this year, he revealed, but called that "normal" and around the EU average.

The problem surrounds what happens next - when the system fails and control of the line shifts to manual.

In this case, the minister highlighted a series of human errors that proved catastrophic.

Crucially, at one point a controller instructed a stalled train to restart, clearing it to advance at up to 160km/h (100 mph) even though a second train was stuck on the line up ahead.

The impending collision was clear from audio calls and on big screens in the control centre in Madrid.

"They worked. We checked. They could see what was happening," Puente confirmed. But the advancing train was never ordered to stop.

"I'm no judge... But these are the facts."

So would he take personal and political responsibility anyway, and resign? Puente called it his "duty", rather, to remain as minister.

"I'll face up to things, explain, elucidate," he countered. "I'll think how to improve the system, and give confidence to those who want to travel by train and feel calm and safe."

But Spaniards will take a lot of persuading.

"This is not only a very serious accident, but the second in a very short time," Paco Camas of the pollster Ipsos points out.

An investigation into January's crash in Adamuz , near Cordoba, is still open, with initial reports suggesting there was a crack in the rails - very different to the latest collision.

"It destroys people's confidence not only in the railways but institutions in general," Camas warns. "And in Spain when such things happen, we know that people blame their government."

For Team Sánchez it is the latest in a spiral of crises.

Allegations of corruption against the prime minister's close relatives still persist, all denied.

Then there was a sudden influx of migrants from Morocco this summer to the Spanish exclave of Ceuta. That got right-wing opponents shouting about incompetence and underfunding.

Later, a video of a pensioner being forcibly evicted from her home went viral and sparked street protests.

His chances of winning the vote looked slim even before the train crash. Now they have plummeted.

Most recent polls showed the centre-right PP coming first and forming a coalition with the far-right Vox.

"They have this majority in almost 95% of the simulations we have done," Prof Pablo Simon of Madrid's Carlos III University explains.

But Sánchez had been running a positive campaign, trying to lure apathetic voters to the polls to vote socialist.

"They've totally lost control of the agenda and the emotion of this campaign," Simon says. "It's going to be extremely difficult now. There is this general mood of decay, of a country that's not working properly. A depression."

There have already been small protests over the train crash led by far-right groups in Madrid and large numbers of police are on stand-by this weekend ahead of further potential clashes, organised online.

"We all travelled in silence and really sad," Paloma told me at the city station, where she had just pulled in on a half empty train.

She admitted she's scared of the high-speed network now and angry at the government.

"This crash will change all of our votes, completely," Paloma said. "We'll shift from the left wing to the right. Because of everything that's happened."

Lucia takes the high-speed AVE into Madrid each day, and is scared too.

"This was human error. But there's been two accidents now with more than 100 dead," she says. "Things here are really bad. They have to change."

Producer Davide Ghiglione contributed to this report

articles.title: In 1971, Stockholm residents climbed 13 elms slated for a subway entrance; mass protests stopped the felling, and the trees survived
articles.summary: In May 1971, mass protests by Stockholm residents prevented the felling of 13 historic elms in Kungsträdgården for a subway entrance, marking a significant event in urban activism that shaped future city planning and preservation efforts.
articles.body: Kungsträdgården is a central garden in Stockholm that has long served as a gathering place. There are cafes under the ancient trees and blocks in and around the park that have already been remodelled a lot as Stockholm developed. In the course of post-war planning, the centre has always been considered a subject of renewal, which included demolition, construction of roads and of new connections between different places of the city. One such connection, implied building a subway and construction of an entrance nearby. That place was occupied by a line of elms and an ancient tea-house. Those people who disapproved of such development did not limit themselves in expressing their opinion in writing letters only. They organized themselves, watched the construction site and when builders came there with saws, some people sat in the branches of the trees.City 67 and the plan to fell 13 elms for a subway entranceAccording to Stockholmskällan, Stockholm’s history portal, the idea emerged in May 1967 when a project called City 67 proposed subway entrances and shops in the park. According to the English- language broadcast of Sveriges Radio celebrating the 40th anniversary of the tree-chopping incident, the town council had previously ordered the demolition of numerous old buildings throughout central Stockholm in efforts to fight poverty, rat infestation and infectious disease. The Sveriges Radio broadcast also reported that an architecture student discovered the tree plan while visiting a classmate in the planning department. Alternative Stad activists got three alternative plans along with this one, where there was no need for the felling of trees and which the city government tried to keep secret; all four plans were posted near the tea house. The municipality insisted that these elms were unhealthy. According to a 2021 Tidningen Syre article marking the 50th anniversary of the protest, the municipality relied on a single assessment, while specialists from Skogshögskolan independently reviewed the trees and found them healthy.The night of 11 to 12 May 1971 and the protesters in the branches The official date for the felling was 13 May and Sveriges Radio notes that the protesters did not trust it, so the workmen arrived earlier, in the night between 11 and 12 May. In her study “Preservation and Protest: Counterculture and Heritage in 1970s Sweden,” published in Future Anterior, Thordis Arrhenius describes workmen arriving with chainsaws early on 12 May, a time chosen to get around protesters who had been camping at the site for several weeks. Thousands of protesters took part and the protest was largely non-violent. Protesters climbed into the trees and Sveriges Radio reports that there was then no reasonable way to disperse them. Thousands of Stockholmers kept up the protest for a whole week, sleeping in tents and hammocks, according to the subway art guide Stockholm Art Walk. Atlas Obscura explains that the majority of the elms are still standing and one of them bears chainsaw marks from that night.What Daniel Helldèn’s 2005 thesis found about the political establishment The doctoral thesis Demokratin utmanas: Almstriden och det politiska etablissemanget, written by Daniel Helldén at Stockholm University and defended in 2005, examines how politicians in central positions in Stockholm and nationally, together with the editorial pages of Stockholm newspapers, understood the conflict. It also questions the reasons for the politicians of the city getting involved in the events and the relation of the social democrats to the radicalization of the late 1960s.In the press release from Stockholm University about the thesis, it is stated that from the perspective of the politicians, the event turned out to be a failure as they had to give way to something that was referred to as parliament of the streets. The press release explains that the party’s hierarchical structure was out of step with the spirit of the time. According to Helldén, in his 2011 interview with Sveriges Radio, the study described above led to permanent changes.Arsenalsgatan 10 and the shift in Swedish planning after 1971Stockholm Art Walk reports that construction was delayed and the entrance eventually received a new address at Arsenalsgatan 10, which left the elms in place. The Library of Congress subject record for the Elm Conflict describes the dispute as one of the first major, concrete, political clashes at the municipal level in Post war, Sweden. In her study mentioned above, Arrhenius argues that the protest marked a turning point, weakening broad support for the modernisation drive begun in the 1930s and for the Social Democratic government’s planning approach. Furthermore, she explained that the shift from the modern impacted the preservation culture of Sweden by widening the definition of historic things. According to a 2011 article in The Local, Ame Fredlund, the assistant director of town planning at the City Council, said the main effect was far greater respect for people’s points of view. Decades later, the trees faced a different threat. According to a 2021 SVT report, the park’s elms were threatened by elm disease and were being treated with vaccinations given through tree syringes.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: A 150-foot historic crane overlooking England’s Cowes waterfront faced the risk of collapse; after years of legal appeals, the council recovered the cost of emergency repairs from its former owners
articles.summary: England's historic Hammerhead Crane in Cowes, Isle of Wight, faced the risk of collapse because of severe corrosion before emergency stabilisation works
articles.body: England's historic Hammerhead Crane in Cowes, Isle of Wight, faced the risk of collapse because of severe corrosion before emergency stabilisation works secured the Grade II* listed structure. After years of legal proceedings and appeals, the Isle of Wight Council recovered £358,000 from the site's former owners to cover the repair costs. According to the council's announcement on 15 June 2026, £348,000 was returned to Historic England after the authority reimbursed its own officer costs. Built in the early 1900s, the 80-tonne crane is the only surviving pre-First World War hammerhead crane of its kind in England.Cowes' historic Hammerhead Crane faced collapse from severe corrosionThe 150-foot Hammerhead Crane dominates the waterfront skyline in Cowes and reflects the Isle of Wight's shipbuilding heritage. According to the Isle of Wight Council, severe corrosion left the landmark at risk of collapse, prompting the authority to issue Urgent Works Notices in 2014 and again in 2016. The council said it intervened after the site's owners failed to take the necessary action to protect the structure. As a Grade II* listed industrial monument, the crane required urgent work to preserve its historic fabric and prevent further deterioration. The council ultimately arranged the stabilisation works itself, using contractors based on the island.Emergency repairs stabilised the 80-tonne listed craneThe council carried out emergency repairs to key components of the crane, including its tower, jib and ballast box. Historic England provided funding for the work, which was intended to stabilise the structure and reduce the risk of collapse. The crane weighs 80 tonnes and was built in the early 1900s, making it a surviving example of the heavy engineering infrastructure associated with Britain's shipbuilding industry. During both world wars, it played a role in Cowes' shipbuilding operations by lifting heavy boilers and engines into naval vessels. Its survival preserves a physical link to the town's industrial and maritime history, while the repairs addressed the structural deterioration that threatened the landmark.Isle of Wight Council recovers £358,000 after legal appealsAfter a series of appeals, the council secured a ruling in 2025 confirming that the former owners of the land were responsible for the emergency repair costs. The authority subsequently recovered £358,000, according to its announcement published on 15 June 2026. After accounting for its officers' costs, the council returned £348,000 to Historic England. The outcome meant that taxpayers were not left to bear the full cost of the emergency intervention. Lee Byrne, the council's conservation projects officer, said the authority had been determined to save the landmark and ensure that the financial responsibility rested with the owners. articles.title: Are the autumns we remember disappearing?
articles.summary: As autumn colours emerge more slowly, experts say changing weather conditions are having an impact.
articles.body:
Frosty Halloween mornings. Bonfire Night wrapped up in hats and gloves. Trees turning red, orange and gold.

For many of us, those are the hallmarks of a traditional autumn.

Yet as October draws to a close, with leaves still clinging to branches and patches of green lingering in parks and woodlands, some people are asking what happened to the autumn they remember.

After one of the hottest and driest summers on record, experts warned some trees had experienced a " false autumn " - shedding leaves early to conserve water rather than following the gradual seasonal process that produces vivid autumn colours.

Few people spend more time watching the seasons change than wildlife photographer Sharon Levi, who owns Brine Pit Wildlife Photography in Droitwich.

The Worcestershire-based photographer said the vivid reds and oranges often associated with autumn had been slower to emerge this year.

"It's like the silver birch trees this year started losing their leaves in the summer when it was hot," she said.

"They've still got some leaves on them, but they've not got as much leaf.

"We haven't got all the vivid reds and oranges that we get but there's a few trees about that are turning now."

So are our autumns really changing, or are we simply remembering the past through rose-tinted glasses?

Prof Dan Bebber, an ecologist at the University of Exeter, said many people would recognise the feeling that autumn no longer looks quite the way it once did.

"If we all think back to our childhoods, and I guess people of my age anyway, it was always freezing cold and frosty for Halloween and 5 November," he said.

"These days, it can be T-shirt weather."

But before getting to what has changed, it helps to understand why leaves fall in the first place.

While evergreen trees, such as pines, keep their needles throughout winter, deciduous trees shed their leaves to conserve energy as temperatures fall and daylight hours shorten.

"There's two ways of dealing with winter," Bebber said.

Evergreen trees "tough it out", while deciduous trees "cut their losses", reabsorbing nutrients from their leaves before dropping them and waiting for spring to return.

Bebber said trees could be thought of as a "solar-powered water fountain", constantly drawing water from the soil and moving it to their leaves.

When there is not enough water in the ground, trees come under stress and are forced to make difficult trade-offs.

"When it gets really dry, trees have to cut their losses and just decide it's too dangerous to even have leaves anymore," he said.

In some cases, that can lead to a false autumn.

"The false autumns tend to have duller colours because it's almost like a rush job and the trees are dropping their leaves without going through that complete absorbance of photosynthesis."

As a result, some trees can lose their leaves before producing the vivid reds, oranges and golds many people associate with autumn.

That does not mean those displays have disappeared altogether.

"If you've got the right kind of conditions where the trees are going through a kind of a real autumn, rather than just shutting off and dropping the leaves due to drought, then you will see that the trees will remove the green from the leaves," Bebber said.

"If you've got a big patch of the same types of species then you'll see those big displays."

Evidence from across England suggests there is no single autumn timetable.

Forestry England's Autumn Leaf Watch tracker suggests the season is unfolding at different speeds across the country. Sightings have been recorded in the New Forest in Hampshire and the Forest of Dean in Gloucestershire.

Reports have also been logged in Delamere Forest in Cheshire, Sherwood Forest in Nottinghamshire, Thetford Forest on the Norfolk-Suffolk border and Dalby Forest in North Yorkshire.

Autumn changes have also been recorded at Cannock Chase Forest in Staffordshire, Haughmond Hill in Shropshire and Hay Wood in Warwickshire.

Forestry England says autumn colours are developing at different rates depending on local weather conditions, elevation and tree species.

That means some woodlands are already glowing gold and orange, while others remain noticeably green.

For Levi, however, the changes extend beyond the colours of the leaves.

"If you go back 30-odd years, we used to have proper winters," she said.

"My children have never seen that and they're in their 30s."

While Bebber believes weather patterns are changing, he is cautious about predicting exactly what that means for future autumns.

"We're entering a period of quite uncertain weather," he said.

"But exactly how they will, I wouldn't want to say."

articles.title: First acts revealed for Shrewsbury Folk Festival's 30th event
articles.summary: Folk legend Richard Thompson is among the first acts announced for the Shrewsbury Folk Festival
articles.body:
Folk legend Richard Thompson, shanty group Fisherman's Friends and African-Afro Cuban pioneers Orchestra Baobab are among the first acts announced for the 30th edition of Shrewsbury Folk Festival.

The four-day event, which began in Bridgnorth in 1997 with 700 festival-goers, will also celebrate 20 years at its current home at the West Mid Showground.

More than a dozen other performers were also unveiled, with organisers promising a mix of folk favourites, new discoveries and exclusive performances.

Created by husband-and-wife team Alan Surtees and Sandra Surtees, the festival outgrew its original Bridgnorth site before moving to Shrewsbury in 2006 and settling at the showground the next year.

What started as a small event has since grown into one of the UK's best-loved folk festivals, according to organisers.

Among the headline acts announced for next year's event is Richard Thompson, who organisers said will perform with a select line-up of musical friends in an exclusive show for the festival.

Also appearing are The Young'uns, Grace Petrie, Fanny Lumsden, Edward II, Hayde Bluegrass Orchestra, Morgan Toney, Grainne Duffy and David Eagle, who will bring his one-man comedy show to the event.

Festival director Sandra Surtees said: "Celebrating 30 years of the festival and 20 years at our showground home is going to be an amazing party.

"The line-up will include some of our favourite artists, some incredible talents never seen before at the festival and some special shows just for Shrewsbury.

"I never imagined in my wildest dreams 30 years ago that the festival would grow into one of the country's most loved folk events."

The festival features four music stages as well as dance events, workshops, craft and music fairs, food stalls and on-site camping and glamping.

Next year's takes place over the August Bank Holiday weekend, from 27-30 August, with more acts due to be announced in the coming months. Tickets are now on sale.

articles.title: Properties adapting to changing nature of storms in South West
articles.summary: The first named storms of the season - Austen and Boelo - caused widespread disruption in the UK.
articles.body:
Extreme weather events including named storms are forcing organisations to adapt their sites to protect themselves and visitors.

Storms Austen and Boelo wreaked havoc and caused disruption across the UK at the end of last week as they brought wind gusts of 85mph (137km/h) and heavy downpours of rain.

Trees were uprooted during the storms, including an incident which led to the death of 60-year-old Richard Baines in Scotland , along with public transport service cancellations and power cuts to thousands of properties.

In south-west England, tourism and council bosses said they were having to battle with the "unpredictability" of the weather as the severity of storms appears to increase.

Several National Trust properties across Devon and Cornwall were forced to close during Storm Austen due to safety concerns.

The charity said the stormy conditions caused widespread disruption at its properties including trees falling at Godolphin and Trengwainton Garden in Cornwall and Lydford Gorge in Devon.

It added part of the roof of the boiler room at Levant Mine near St Just in Cornwall suffered damaged while power cuts and fires were also reported across some sites.

Gareth Lay, general manager for Heart of Cornwall portfolio group at the National Trust which looks after properties including Trelissick and Trerice, said the damage from Austen had compounded issues caused earlier this year by Storm Goretti.

He said his team was trying to learn from what had happened during the storms in order to future proof the historic buildings, but there was only so much they could do.

"What we are seeing is an increase in the number of storms and an increase in severity of these storms," Lay said.

"It's really giving us a significant challenge in terms of how we can better plant or manage our properties to protect us from those storms.

"It's quite tricky to find new ways and different ways in how we can adapt the physical parts of our building to be more resilient to these storms."

Bosses at the Eden Project have also been considering how to keep their site safe for staff and visitors during stormy weather.

In the past, the venue in a former clay pit near St Austell has experienced landslips as a result of bad weather .

Phil Young, a horticultural manager at the site, said while the garden was relatively well protected from the elements, they did have to consider how to make it safer.

He said this included looking at the resilience of its tree stock and planting species with deeper roots.

"What I think we consider is unpredictability," Young said.

"That is where I'd say we're looking way, way, way into the future to make sure our plant collections and our site are adaptable."

He added wintry conditions could be just as problematic.

"I used to live 16 miles away from the site and one year a particularly hard snow storm came out of the blue and it took me four hours to get home," Young said.

East Devon District Council said it had a number of issues reported during Austen including debris such as sand and pebbles being blown on to seafront promenades.

Councillor Geoff Jung, portfolio holder for environment operations, said the authority had to deal with the "double whammy" of preparing for climate change and rising sea levels at the same time.

He said projects including a £21m coastal defence scheme for Sidmouth had been lined up to help deal with the impact of severe weather conditions.

Jung added protecting the district was difficult as the Jurassic Coast - a world heritage site - ran through it.

"In some ways, you've got to consider it like the Taj Mahal in India," Jung said.

"If we had the Taj Mahal, would we be coating it with concrete to protect it?

"So we have to look at it very carefully and we have to go through a lot of hoops to do any work on the Jurassic Coast."

articles.title: One dead, 6 injured in shooting inside Spirit Halloween at California shopping mall
articles.summary: One person was killed and six others were injured in a shooting at a Spirit Halloween store packed with last-minute Halloween shoppers on Friday night.
articles.body:
One person was killed and six others were injured in a shooting at a Spirit Halloween store in California packed with last-minute Halloween shoppers on Friday night.

Gunfire rang out inside the seasonal retail store at the Solano Town Center mall in Fairfield, Calif., at around 8:30 p.m., Fairfield Police Chief Dan Marshall said during a press conference.

One person was pronounced dead at the scene, while six others were rushed to a hospital, where three are listed in critical condition.

Police did not reveal any description of the suspected shooter, who remains at large, and did not confirm if there were more than one suspect.

A motive behind the shooting was not revealed.

"This is still a very active crime scene. Detectives are speaking with witnesses and diligently working to identify the suspect responsible for this horrific shooting," police said in a press release.

The ages and identities of the victims were not immediately released.

The store was open and filled with customers when the shooting began, sending shoppers fleeing for their lives.

"Well, she just told me she heard some shots and the people running, yelling and crying already," one witness described what his wife experienced to KCRA.

The man said his wife heard roughly seven shots ring out before bystanders raced to safety, heading out into the parking lots and further into the mall.

The temporary, pop-up Halloween store took over the space once occupied by Best Buy at the mall that holds approximately 130 stores.

"I was in Chipotle a girl working in Spirit ran in & said they came in & just started shooting," one person said, according to the Vacaville Reporter.

SWAT teams worked their way through the mall, checking all areas to see if the shooters were hiding inside.

One of the sweeps was conducted in the Regal Edwards movie theater, where about a dozen people had been watching a showing of the horror film "Halloween."

"Towards the end of the film and all of a sudden a police officer in full SWAT gear came storming in and he had a very large Maglite and he started waving it all over the theater and asked us if anyone came in that had a gun," Caitlin Fry told CBS Sacramento.

Moviegoers said the scary scene inside the theater brought back heartbreaking images from the Aurora mass shooting, where 12 people were killed.

"I was afraid after (the SWAT officer) came in, I thought about 'Dark Knight' in Colorado — the shooting that happened there years ago," Fry's partner Marty McCoy said.

"I told her I don't know what's going to happen when we walk out of here, just remember 'run, hide, fight' and I love you just in case."

Multiple agencies were sending agents to the mall to help with the investigation and search for the suspect, including the FBI.

"FBI Sacramento is aware of the shooting incident that occurred at a business on Gateway Boulevard in Fairfield, California, and we are deploying our Evidence Response Team to assist the Fairfield Police Department," the

The shooting at the Fairfield Spirit Halloween store follows hours after a man was fatally shot in a Michigan store.

The unidentified 21-year-old was found suffering from multiple gunshot wounds at the store in Madison Heights just after 2 p.m., according to the Madison Heights Police Department.

Another 21-year-old, suspected in the killing, was attacked by bystanders and taken to the hospital while in police custody.

articles.title: US, South Korea, Japan call for ‘complete denuclearisation’ of North Korea
articles.summary: The joint statement comes as US President Donald Trump seeks a new meeting with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.
articles.body:
The United States, South Korea and Japan have reiterated their longstanding call for North Korea to give up its nuclear weapons, a move Pyongyang has repeatedly ruled out.

The three countries addressed the issue on the sidelines of the Group of 20 (G20) meeting in the US city of Atlanta on Thursday, with their top diplomats reaffirming their “resolute commitment to the complete denuclearisation” of North Korea, according to a readout by the US Department of State.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun and Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi also pledged the “full implementation” of United Nations Security Council resolutions, including a ban on supporting revenue for North Korea’s nuclear and ballistic missile programmes.

The statement comes despite repeated overtures to North Korea by US President Donald Trump, who held a series of historic summits with its leader, Kim Jong Un, during his first term in office and has continued to call Kim a “friend” .

Last year, Trump bucked a long-held US policy by conceding that North Korea was already “sort of a nuclear power”.

More recently, he has played down concerns about North Korea’s nuclear programme and expressed a desire to meet Kim again. Speculation is mounting that the two leaders could reconnect at next month’s APEC summit in China, which Trump is due to attend.

Analysts and South Korea’s spy agency say Kim may have conveyed Pyongyang’s position on potential talks with Trump to Beijing during a recent visit to the Chinese border city of Dandong.

South Korea’s dovish President Lee Jae Myung – who has repeatedly offered Pyongyang talks without preconditions – suggested in September that Washington seek a freeze, rather than the immediate elimination, of the North’s nuclear programme in return for sanctions relief.

Critics have said such an approach risks tacitly accepting North Korea as a nuclear-armed state while allowing Pyongyang to win sanctions relief without giving up its arsenal.

Despite long-running UN sanctions, North Korea, which is backed by Russia and China, has enshrined its status as a nuclear-armed state in law. Pyongyang’s government has declared its atomic arsenal to be permanent and irreversible.

Pyongyang denounced a joint statement on Saturday by a group of nations monitoring sanctions implementation against it, pledging that “the stereotyped sanctions racket of the US and the West can neither influence the position of the DPRK (North Korea) as a nuclear weapons state.”

articles.title: ‘How is everyone surviving?’: Bengaluru man says family of four spends up to Rs 80,000 a month on  groceries and food, sparking debate over rising food costs
articles.summary: For many households, grocery shopping is a routine expense.
articles.body: For many households, grocery shopping is a routine expense. But when the monthly bill starts approaching the cost of a holiday or a major purchase, it can quickly become a talking point. That is what happened after Bengaluru-based social media user Ramsri Goutham Golla shared that his family of four spends between Rs 60,000 and Rs 80,000 every month on groceries and food, despite preparing all their meals at home.His post raised a question that many people could relate to: how much does it really cost to feed a family comfortably today? While some users said the amount reflected the rising cost of food and the expense of eating well, others felt the figure was unusually high and questioned the family's spending habits. The discussion soon turned into a comparison of household budgets, with people from different cities sharing how much they spend on groceries each month.A home-cooked food budget that surprised social media usersGolla explained that his household includes two adults and two young children. The family prepares its meals at home and includes meat in its diet twice a week. Despite not depending entirely on restaurant meals or food deliveries, he said the monthly grocery and food bill remains between Rs 60,000 and Rs 80,000. Sharing his frustration, he wrote, “Groceries and food cost Rs 60K–Rs 80K a month for us with 2 adults and 2 young kids, with everything cooked at home and meat twice a week! How is everyone surviving?”The post prompted people to look more closely at their own spending. Some said they had also noticed grocery expenses increasing, while others admitted that they rarely calculated how much they spent on food every month. One user said the post had made them reconsider their expenses, writing, “I did not realise the cost until I saw this. Time for a reality check. We order food online as well.”Another person agreed that food prices had become more difficult to manage, saying, “It’s true if someone said a few years back I would not believe it but nowadays prices are higher and higher.” A user from Hyderabad also supported Golla's point, saying that feeding a family of four with healthy food could easily cost more than Rs 60,000 a month. Golla responded that he would be happy if his expenses stayed at that level, adding that his actual bill was even higher.Eggs, milk, meat and fruits: Where does the money go?As the discussion continued, users began questioning how a family could spend so much on groceries. Some argued that even good-quality food and regular meat consumption should not push a household's monthly kitchen budget that high. One person challenged the estimate, claiming that a family of four in Bengaluru could manage its kitchen expenses within Rs 15,000 to Rs 20,000, even while buying premium food products and meat.Golla then offered a breakdown of some of his regular purchases to explain why the bill adds up. According to him, eggs alone cost around Rs 3,000 a month because the family consumes an average of 10 eggs daily. Milk adds another Rs 2,000 to Rs 3,000, while meat purchased twice a week costs approximately Rs 6,000 to Rs 8,000.He also listed dosa and idli batter, which he said costs between Rs 2,000 and Rs 3,000 monthly. Other expenses include rice, fruits, vegetables, cooking oil, tea powder, dry fruits and nuts. Pointing to the price of everyday food items, Golla said rice costs around Rs 80 per kg, while fruits can cost Rs 200 to Rs 400 or more per kg. Vegetables such as onions, tomatoes, okra and potatoes add to the total. His explanation shifted the discussion from the overall monthly figure to the cost of individual items that households buy regularly.Families share their own monthly grocery budgetsNot everyone agreed that a family of four needs to spend anywhere close to Rs 80,000 on food. Several users shared their own budgets, suggesting that the amount varies depending on the city, food choices and household requirements. A user from a prime suburb in Mumbai said their household of four adults and a dog spends around Rs 50,000 a month, including daily non-vegetarian food. articles.title: How Bristol became the home of drum and bass and jungle
articles.summary: Artists inspired by sound systems, acid house and hip hop changed the course of dance music forever.
articles.body:
It has been more than 30 years since Bristol with a "rebel" mentality ventured into the unknown, giving birth to the global phenomenon that is jungle and drum and bass music.

The city is still a heavyweight on the scene, inspiring generations of artists to continue pushing boundaries in dance music.

Jungle continues to be developed by artists across London and Bristol, but in its beginnings the sound from Bristol was more expansive and experimental.

It all started in the early 90s, with a DJ collective called Full Cycle . They were influenced by Jamaican sound systems, acid house and hip hop, which led to a new sound explosion in the city.

How Bristol shaped Maya Jama before her TV fame

Bristol then and now: Trams, barges and rugby

Apology after two women's rights campaigners banned

DJ Krust - who was part of the collective - said the music was about "finding expression through our artform which was DJing and producing".

"Rave culture was a huge factor in speeding the tempo up. Once it got to 160bpm and now it's 170bpm, that felt like home for us," he said.

The jungle music they had a hand in creating is still to this day characterised by its speed, syncopated rhythms, breakbeats and ragga, funk and reggae samples.

The Full Cycle collective showcased their new music on the streets at St Paul's Carnival and when they saw people liked it, they made more.

Krust said the beginnings of jungle and drum and bass were a partnership between the open mindedness of the city, the creativity of these DJs and their proximity to rave culture at free parties in the West Country countryside.

"We had to explore and dig deep to hear and see how this experiment can work in real time - that was huge to see," he said.

"When we finally figured out jungle we found our voice," he added.

The collective was made up of DJ Krust, DJ Die, producer Roni Size and DJ Suv - from Krust's original band Fresh Four, best-known for the top 10 hit Wishing on a Star .

By this time, Full Cycle had a show on commercial radio station Galaxy Radio - something Krust said became a really "pivotal moment" for the collective.

"It was like the calling for the youth - here you go, here's your new soundtrack, it's British and it's the sound of the streets," Krust said.

"You could feel it in the air that we'd got something and it was travelling through word of mouth - something was brewing and we could all feel it.

"This was the movement, this was the shift," he added.

In 1997, Full Cycle formed the live act Reprazent and released the album 'New Forms' which included the hit track Brown Paper Bag .

Later that year they made history by becoming the first drum and bass group to win the Mercury Prize - firmly putting Bristol, jungle and drum and bass on the musical map.

Jungle went on to become the precursor to drum and bass music which is also fast, but has a signature simple kick and snare pattern that sits over rolling basslines.

The two genres are sometimes used interchangeably, but both still have a distinct sound.

DJ Die, who was also a member of Full Cycle, said Bristol was at the heart of the movement because of its "rebel" and "do it yourself mentality".

"It hasn't seemed to have died yet, it's more healthy than ever. A lot of people move to Bristol for the music scene," he said.

"There's so many great producers here, there always have been - it's a hotbed for production," he added.

DJ Die attributed the longevity of the city's jungle scene to sound systems that have been passed down through generations and new talent inspired by Bristol's artists.

"You've got these grassroots soundsystems handed down from old ravers like Spiral Tribe," he said.

"You've also got to shout out St Paul's because that's had such a big influence and the Jamaican community there."

The scene is thriving now more than ever as new artists such as Nia Archives - who was discovered by DJ Die - make waves in the industry.

Nia's second album was shortlisted for the Mercury Awards, she headlined Bristol festival Love Saves the Day in 2025 and had also played a number of the biggest festivals in the UK, including Glastonbury.

Another artist continuing the city's legacy is Sherelle.

She said DJ Die and DJ Krust were direct influences on her high-tempo music, which includes a blend of footwork, jungle and drum and bass.

"If you were to separate Die, Krust and Roni from everyone, they have their own individual sound and when they come together, it also builds on another sound," she said.

"Bristol is such an off-kilter place. It's a place whereby exploration is so expansive.

"The city is rich in cultural undertones and you can tell that they're making music from the heart.

"There needs to be a lot of focus and emphasis about actually how special and important Bristol is to the current music, culture and climate that we've got now," she said.

Roni Size and Reprazent will perform their seminal album New Forms live across the UK next year to celebrate 30 years since its release.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed the launch, saying the service would save time and improve the travel experience for passengers.In a post on X, the Prime Minister described the development as a historic day for passengers travelling between Delhi and Kashi.“Today is a historic day for those traveling by rail between Delhi and Kashi. With the launch of the Kashi-Delhi Vande Bharat Sleeper Train, not only will there be a saving of time, but their experience is also set to improve. Equipped with modern amenities and a state-of-the-art safety system, this is the country’s second Vande Bharat Sleeper Train,” he wrote.In another post, Modi highlighted the route's significance for pilgrims, tourists and business travellers, noting that the train would connect several important destinations across Uttar Pradesh.“The Vande Bharat Sleeper train running from Kashi to Prayagraj, via Kanpur Central, to Delhi will make travel convenient for millions of devotees, tourists, youth, and businesspeople,” he said.Emphasising the cultural and religious importance of the route, the Prime Minister added, “Whether it’s a darshan of Baba Vishwanath or a journey to the Sangam, this train will connect faith with opportunity and tradition with modernity.
